Disclosure, litigation sentence (FACT): 'the Pentagon labeled Anthropic a supply-chain risk after it refused to drop limits on military use of its models; a federal judge in California called the label unlawful retaliation in August, and the D.C. Circuit let it stand in September.' There were two designations, not one label. Hegseth issued two designation letters in March 2026, one under 10 U.S.C. 3252 and one under FASCSA (41 U.S.C. 4713). Judge Lin's Aug. 27 ruling addressed the 3252 designation; the D.C. Circuit (2-1, Sept. 25) upheld the FASCSA designation (Tech Times; ABC). The page makes one label sound both struck and upheld. My round-1 fix wording had the same conflation. The refusal ('written assurances that Claude would not be used for fully autonomous lethal weapons or mass domestic surveillance') is supported by Tech Times and TechCrunch.
verdicts.fix: ...which is in litigation with Hegseth's department: the Pentagon designated Anthropic a supply-chain risk under two laws after it refused to drop limits on military use of its models. A federal judge in California held one designation unlawful retaliation in August; the D.C. Circuit upheld the other in September.
